description: We are Everything Is Possible, a team driven by curiosity, creativity, and innovation. Our interests include space exploration, astronomy, aerospace technology, AI, and web development. We are developing Abandoned, But Not Forgotten, an interactive educational storybook about human missions to the Moon and Mars, featuring visual storytelling and English and Hindi narration. We welcome beginners and experienced contributors interested in research, coding, design, animation, and content creation.
summary:
Abandoned, But Not Forgotten ("Red Horizon: The Mars Chronicles") is an interactive, zero-dependency 3D educational space storybook deployed live at [https://abandoned-but-not-forgotten-storybook.pages.dev](https://abandoned-but-not-forgotten-storybook.pages.dev) for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

What We Developed
Built with client-side web standards (HTML5, CSS3, ES6+ JavaScript, Web Speech API), the platform transforms dense technical mission archives into an emotional, multi-sensory journey across 13 historical chapters, 82 3D scenes, and 446 bilingual narrative passages in English and Hindi. Players experience real exploration missions from the first-person perspective of the machines themselves—such as Apollo Lunar Module descent stages, nuclear ALSEP stations, electric lunar rovers, and Mars pioneers—supported by synchronized subtitles, real-time speech narration, and 82 interactive hotspots revealing spacecraft mechanics, scientific discoveries, and lasting legacies.
details:
Project Solution While active rovers capture headlines, humanity's earliest robotic pioneers resting on the Moon and Mars are often forgotten by younger generations. Abandoned, But Not Forgotten ("Red Horizon: The Mars Chronicles") is an interactive, zero-dependency 3D educational space storybook deployed live at [https://abandoned-but-not-forgotten-storybook.pages.dev](https://abandoned-but-not-forgotten-storybook.pages.dev) that brings these historic machines back to life—allowing learners to experience space exploration from the first-person perspective of the landers, rovers, and orbital probes themselves.

Main landing interface introducing learners to the interactive 3D lunar and Martian mission chronicles.

How Does Our Solution Work? Built with pure client-side web standards (HTML5, CSS3, ES6+ JavaScript, Web Speech API), the platform transforms dense space agency telemetry archives into a multi-sensory, self-paced STEM experience across 13 historical chapters and 82 interactive 3D scenes:

  • First-Person Bilingual Storytelling (English & Hindi): Features 446 narrative passages spoken from the machines' viewpoints—covering Apollo Lunar Module descent stages, nuclear ALSEP stations, electric lunar rovers, and Mars pioneers—supported by synchronized subtitles and real-time voice synthesis.

Interactive 3D chapter view featuring first-person spacecraft narration and synchronized bilingual subtitles.

  • Interactive Mechanical & Scientific Hotspots: Users explore 82 clickable hotspots directly on the 3D spacecraft models to inspect hardware subsystems, power sources (such as SNAP-27 RTGs and solar arrays), scientific instruments, and engineering legacies.

Interactive spacecraft hotspot inspection revealing hardware subsystems, power architecture, and mission telemetry.

  • Verified Planetary & Lunar Telemetry: Grounded in authentic spacecraft identifiers, dry mass specifications, landing coordinates, and crew EVA transcripts compiled from NASA NSSDCA, the Apollo Lunar Surface Journal (ALSJ), LRO surveys, ISRO's Mangalyaan (MOM) telemetry, and ESA's Planetary Science Archive.

Historical Mars exploration chapter highlighting surface discoveries, rover mobility logs, and planetary telemetry.

  • Zero-Dependency Classroom Accessibility: Engineered without heavy external frameworks so students on any browser or low-bandwidth connection can launch chapters instantly with zero downloads.

Lunar exploration chapter showcasing Apollo surface hardware, ALSEP instruments, and LRO orbital verification context.

Bilingual accessibility mode delivering STEM narration and technical archives in Hindi and English.

The Simulator Benefits & Our Goal

  • Preserves Spaceflight Heritage: Connects younger audiences emotionally with the robotic explorers that paved the way for Artemis and future human Mars missions.
  • Bridges Language Barriers in STEM: Provides native bilingual narration and subtitles in both English and Hindi to make verified NASA and ISRO scientific data accessible worldwide.
  • Turns Archives into Active Learning: Replaces static data tables with interactive 3D exploration and verbatim mission communications.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • Core Web Architecture: Zero-dependency HTML5, CSS3, and ES6+ JavaScript (js/mars-story-data.js and js/moon-story-data.js).
  • Audio & Accessibility: Native Web Speech API for real-time bilingual voice synthesis and synchronized text captions.
  • Hosting & Version Control: Cloudflare Pages Edge CDN ([https://abandoned-but-not-forgotten-storybook.pages.dev](https://abandoned-but-not-forgotten-storybook.pages.dev)) and GitHub ([https://github.com/bhawsarhardik195-blip/Abandoned-But-Not-Forgotten](https://github.com/bhawsarhardik195-blip/Abandoned-But-Not-Forgotten)).
